name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Rabb's large fundraising and outside support
model.rationale: This Philadelphia-based seat carries a D+40 lean, and the only general-election opponent is an independent who has raised about $10,800. Rabb's primary win plus heavy outside spending and markets pricing near certainty make a Democratic hold overwhelming.
model.watch: A surprise independent surge or unusual local dynamics are the only plausible paths to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 3rd District, anchored in Philadelphia, is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, and state Representative Chris Rabb emerges as the Democratic nominee after a well-funded primary, backed by more than $1.5 million in outside support. The general-election field is essentially nominal: Dennis Mahoney, an independent, has raised under $11,000 and has no outside backing.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 99 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling and no meaningful opposition spending, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a Democratic hold by a wide margin.
